sections.question: Can tourists buy weed in Chicago?
sections.short: Yes, if you are 21 or older and show a valid ID. Visitors can buy at any licensed Illinois dispensary.

points.text: Adults 21 and older with a valid identification can buy cannabis at any Illinois dispensary.
The City of Chicago’s cannabis FAQ gives the same rule: adults over 21, with a valid ID.
The State of Illinois licenses dispensaries, and the City of Chicago regulates where they may locate.
At a licensed dispensary, every person who enters has their ID checked, and customers may be checked again before a sale.

sections.question: How much weed can a visitor have in Illinois?
sections.short: Visitors 21 and older can have up to 30 grams of flower, 500 mg of THC in infused products and 5 grams of concentrate. Illinois residents can have twice that. A 2026 law doubled both sets of limits, effective June 12, 2026.

points.text: Public Act 104-0463 (Senate Bill 3222), signed on June 12, 2026 and in effect that day, doubled the possession limits in Section 10-10 of the Illinois Cannabis Regulation and Tax Act (410 ILCS 705/10-10).

Non-residents 21 and older may now have 30 grams of cannabis flower (about 1 ounce), 500 milligrams of THC in cannabis-infused products and 5 grams of cannabis concentrate, up from 15 grams, 250 milligrams and 2.5 grams.

Illinois residents 21 and older may now have 60 grams of flower (about 2 ounces), 1,000 milligrams of THC in infused products and 10 grams of concentrate, up from 30 grams, 500 milligrams and 5 grams.
The totals are cumulative: an adult may have a combination of flower, infused products and concentrate, up to the limit for each kind of product.

If you look up the statute itself: the Illinois General Assembly’s online compiled text of Section 10-10 had not been updated when checked on November 27, 2026, and still showed the limits from before the 2026 law.

sections.question: Where can you smoke weed in Chicago?
sections.short: On private property where the owner allows it. Not in public, including streets, parks and the area next to a dispensary, and not in any vehicle.

points.text: Consumption in public is illegal in Chicago, and that includes streets, parks and areas next to dispensaries.

Illinois law doesn’t let anyone smoke, vape, eat or otherwise use cannabis in any public place: any place where you could reasonably be expected to be seen by others, and any place owned or leased by the state or a local government, such as parks and government buildings.
Consumption on private property is permitted, at the property owner’s discretion.

State law also bars using it close to anyone under 21 who isn’t a registered medical patient, and bars even having it on school grounds, in a school bus or on any federal property, including military bases, federal parks and federal buildings.

sections.question: How can I tell a Chicago dispensary is licensed?
sections.short: Look it up on the state’s dispensary map, and look for what Illinois requires of every licensed store: a posted state license, an ID check at the door and tested, labeled products.

points.text: Illinois keeps a map and list of dispensaries that you can search by city, county or zip code.

link.label: Find a dispensary on the state’s map

points.text: A licensed dispensary displays its official license to operate from the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation, and its agent in charge wears an agent identification card issued by the department.
A locked door, opened only by an employee or security guard, separates the entrance from the sales area, and exterior windows are opaque or tinted.
Products show lab test results on the package and have no cannabis leaf or flower on the label. No cannabis flower is on display, and no nicotine products are sold.

sections.question: Can I use cannabis in a car, or drive after using it?
sections.short: No. Cannabis can’t be used in any vehicle, and in a moving car it must be in a sealed, odor-proof, child-resistant container. Driving high is a DUI.

points.text: Cannabis cannot be used in a motor vehicle. Chicago adds that this holds whether or not the vehicle is running.

While a motor vehicle is in operation, cannabis must be in a secured, sealed, odor-proof, child-resistant container in its original packaging. Carrying it in any other kind of container is a Class A misdemeanor.
Driving under the influence of cannabis is illegal and is a DUI.
Illinois prohibits driving or being in control of a vehicle when THC levels of 5 nanograms in whole blood, or 10 nanograms in another bodily substance, are present within 2 hours of driving.

sections.question: Can I fly home with weed from Chicago?
sections.short: Don’t. Illinois says cannabis shouldn’t be taken across state lines, and federal law still applies at airport security.

points.text: Cannabis should not be transported across state lines. Giving it to someone who is leaving the state may put that person in violation of federal and, potentially, other states’ laws.

TSA says marijuana and some cannabis products, including some CBD oil, remain illegal under federal law unless they have no more than 0.3% THC on a dry-weight basis or are FDA-approved. Its officers don’t search for drugs, but they refer anything illegal they find to law enforcement.

sections.question: Does Illinois accept medical cannabis cards from other states?
sections.short: No. Illinois does not accept out-of-state medical cards, but adults 21 and older can buy at adult-use dispensaries with a valid ID.

points.text: Illinois does not accept out-of-state medical cards.
The state’s medical program issues registry cards to Illinois residents who meet its requirements.
Adults 21 and older with a valid identification can buy cannabis at any Illinois dispensary.

sections.question: How long does an edible take to kick in?
sections.short: Longer than you might think: 30 minutes or more before you feel anything, and often 2 to 4 hours for the full effect. Wait before taking more.

points.text: With edibles, you might not feel the effects for 30 minutes or more.
Many people won’t feel the full effect of their dose until 2 to 4 hours after eating it.
